applicability.scope: Engines with multi-token speculative decoding whose verification forward cost grows with query rows
applicability.prerequisites: A calibrated per-position acceptance signal; a measured (rows, step_time) curve; a handle on metadata construction
applicability.hardware: Backend-independent procedure; the reference implementation targets NVIDIA SM100 and Ascend 950 only
applicability.input_contract: Draft width and row representation, the defined individual/conditional versus cumulative acceptance semantics, verify rows/time curve, sampler cost and acceptance round actually available at schedule time.
applicability.produced_artifact: A per-step verification row budget, per-request query lengths from one through draft_width plus one, cumulative acceptance vectors and predicted-versus-realized acceptance error logs.
applicability.failure_modes: Confusing verification savings with reduced drafting, misreading confidence semantics or available rounds, allowing later-position confidence to select an earlier token, or generating non-prefix grants can invalidate the budget or sampling claim.
applicability.refusal_point: Stop if unthrottled drafting or sampler cost dominates, the signal cannot be made cumulative, or no round supplies acceptance estimates; the procedure also does not apply without a per-step cost model.

limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation and no reproduced gain.
The reference budgets verification rows only; draft compute is unchanged.
The budgeted path is off by default in the reference source.
Budgeting can lower accepted length; equal accepted length is not an acceptance criterion.
Per-position independence of the confidence used for verification is a correctness requirement, not only a scheduling convenience.
Cross-backend rejection-comparison parity is unproven; the reference has no equality assertion.
Numeric acceptance rates and warmup curves are deployment-specific and are not carried here.
recommendations: Measure draft, verify and sampler costs separately and fit the verify curve for graph sizes that will actually replay.
Preserve the one-row floor and prefix grants, and audit CPU/GPU allocation timing against the per-position decision-independence contract.
Report verification rows, accepted tokens, total step time and throughput separately; use an independently specified sampling oracle rather than requiring unchanged accepted length.
